issues.detail: The Greek 'εν πνευματι ακαθαρτω' (in an unclean spirit) is rendered as 'bị tà linh ô uế ám' (possessed by an unclean spirit). While theologically similar, the Greek denotes a state of being 'in' a spirit, whereas the Vietnamese adds the concept of 'ám' (possession/haunting), which is not explicitly in the text.

The Greek verb 'ανεκραξεν' is an aorist indicative (he cried out/shouted). The Vietnamese 'liền kêu la lên' uses 'liền' (then/immediately), which implies a sequential progression or immediate reaction not present in the simple narrative tense of the Greek.
